who_they_are: Students in class 11, class 12 or the year straight after, plus anyone in their first year of college. Often the parent is in the conversation too.
what_they_want: A clear answer to what to do after school, and confidence that they are not making a mistake that costs three years.
whats_stopping_them: They cannot compare CA, CFA, ACCA and a plain degree. Their parents are paying and are not convinced. Board exams are consuming everything.
how_to_spot_them: Age or class stated on the form, a school event as the source, or questions about what to do after 12th.
what_to_offer: Career direction first, then the entry level product that actually fits: CA Foundation, ACCA Knowledge, or a comparison if they are still choosing.
what_to_say: Sequencing. Which qualification to start when, and what it costs across the whole route, not just the first year.
what_not_to_say: Do not talk about placements or salaries. Do not create deadline pressure. Do not lead with fees.
next_action: Send the career assessment. When they answer, send the comparison for the two options they shortlisted. Bring the parent in at step 3, never step 1.
cadence: One message every 5 to 7 days. Pause completely during board exams.
owner: System until a parent joins the conversation
exit_rule: Three unanswered messages, then park with a return date at the board results window.
advanced_rules: Parent asset must not appear before step 3. Minor consent rules apply below 18.

who_they_are: Second year, final year, recent graduates and job seekers. The clock is running on placements.
what_they_want: To be employable. Something concrete they can show in an interview.
whats_stopping_them: They do not know which role they want, so no course seems obviously right. They cannot judge which credential recruiters actually value.
how_to_spot_them: Final year or graduate status, a campus event source, or any question about jobs, placements or internships.
what_to_offer: Skills first for a short horizon, qualification first for a long one. Analyst Stack or Financial Modelling for the former, CFA Level 1 for the latter.
what_to_say: Roles, not courses. What the job actually involves and what gets screened in an interview.
what_not_to_say: Do not name a course before they name a role. Do not promise placements. Do not send long theory content during placement season.
next_action: Send the skills check. When it is completed, send the gap report and the practical class for their weakest area, then call.
priority: Automated until the skills check is done, then Call this week
cadence: One message every 3 to 4 days. Suspend during placement weeks.
owner: System, then a counsellor once a role is named
exit_rule: Three unanswered messages, then park until placement season ends.
advanced_rules: Course is never named before a role is named. Placement claims require a verified source.

cohort_name: Working professional who knows what they want
who_they_are: People in jobs who named a course and a rough timeline. Also career switchers and anyone who already decided.
what_they_want: To know whether it is doable alongside their job, and then to get on with it.
whats_stopping_them: Time, not money. They have been told a course is hard and want to judge the teaching for themselves.
how_to_spot_them: A job title, a named course, a question about batches, fees or instalments.
what_to_offer: The variant that matches their real weekly hours, then the batch, then the price.
what_to_say: Feasibility. How many hours it really takes, which variant fits, and whether their target attempt is honest.
what_not_to_say: No career guides. No quizzes. No roadmaps. Nothing that reads as a stall when they asked a direct question.
next_action: Ask the hours question with tappable ranges. Send the sample class. Confirm the attempt and batch. Answer the fee with a number.
cadence: Every 2 days while active, then a dated return.
owner: Counsellor from the first transactional question
exit_rule: Two call attempts in different windows, then a dated return.
advanced_rules: Educational content is suppressed entirely. A fee question is answered with a number in the same message, never deferred to a call.

who_they_are: Anyone who failed or deferred an attempt and is deciding whether to try again.
what_they_want: To understand what actually went wrong, so the next attempt is different.
whats_stopping_them: Confidence. Money already spent. A real fear of repeating the outcome.
how_to_spot_them: A stated failure, a deferred attempt, or a record of a prior attempt.
what_to_offer: A topic diagnostic first. Then either partial topics if the gaps are narrow, or the full programme if they are broad.
what_to_say: Diagnosis. Which topics cost the marks, and what changes in the plan because of that.
what_not_to_say: Never mention the failure in the opening. No sympathy language. Do not blame their previous provider unless they raise it first.
next_action: Offer the twenty question diagnostic. If they name their weak topics instead, skip the diagnostic and send the sessions for those topics.
cadence: Every 3 days, anchored to the registration deadline.
owner: System, then a counsellor after the diagnostic
exit_rule: Three unanswered messages, then park until 21 days before the next registration deadline.
advanced_rules: Diagnosis always precedes any product offer. Deadlines quoted must be real published dates.

cohort_name: We do not know what they want yet
who_they_are: Anyone whose course is unknown after enrichment. The largest group in most weeks.
what_they_want: Unclear. That is the point of the playbook.
whats_stopping_them: They do not know enough to ask a specific question, so a course pitch bounces off.
how_to_spot_them: No course named, and nothing in the source that implies one.
what_to_offer: Nothing yet. Establish life stage, then objective, then recommend two options with reasons.
what_to_say: One question at a time, with tappable options and a stated reason for asking.
what_not_to_say: Do not send a course list. Do not send a brochure. Do not ask more than one question.
next_action: Ask studying or working. Their answer selects the real playbook.
advanced_rules: Maximum three profiling questions in total across the lifetime, then stop asking.

who_they_are: Anyone who asked for a fee, a batch date, an instalment plan or a payment link, or who started a checkout.
what_they_want: To complete a purchase without friction.
whats_stopping_them: Usually a practical blocker: the price, the timing, or a payment that failed.
how_to_spot_them: Any transactional question, a checkout event, or a payment failure.
what_to_offer: The exact variant they are buying, at the confirmed price.
what_not_to_say: No education. No nurture. No new content of any kind.
next_action: Confirm the variant and price in one message, then issue the link. Stay on the line through checkout for high value orders.
cadence: Same day, up to three touches.
exit_rule: Payment completed, or a captured objection.
advanced_rules: No payment link without a confirmed variant, price and eligibility. A failed payment is a service problem before it is a sales problem.

who_they_are: Anyone who stopped responding, at any stage.
what_they_want: Unknown. That is what the playbook is trying to establish.
whats_stopping_them: Depends on the silence type. Wrong number, wrong time, wrong ask, or a real blocker they have not said out loud.
how_to_spot_them: No inbound signal for the stage threshold.
what_to_offer: Nothing new. Change the ask, not the offer.
what_to_say: Either a shorter version of the same thing, or a direct question naming the three likely blockers.
what_not_to_say: Never write just following up, checking in, or gentle reminder.
next_action: Work down the silence ladder. If they were ever high intent, a person calls instead of sending a fourth message.
priority: Automated, unless intent ever crossed 61, then Call this week
cadence: 48 to 72 hours between rungs. Three rungs maximum.
owner: System, or a counsellor for previously hot leads
key_resources: None. Assets have already failed once.
exit_rule: Three attempts, then the exit message and park.
advanced_rules: Silence is four different signals and each gets a different response. See the silence ladder.

who_they_are: Anyone parked for more than 30 days.
what_they_want: Nothing right now. Something may have changed.
whats_stopping_them: Whatever stopped them the first time, which is on record.
how_to_spot_them: Parked, with a genuinely new fact available that matches their recorded objection.
what_to_offer: Whatever the new fact is about: a new batch, a scholarship window, a result, an event.
what_to_say: What changed since we last spoke, in one line, with an explicit exit offered.
what_not_to_say: Never send a check in with no news. Never reuse the message that failed the first time.
next_action: Send one message built on the new fact. If they reply, re enter the playbook for their current life stage, not the one recorded a year ago.
cadence: 45 days minimum between attempts. Two attempts in 180 days.
key_resources: R40 plus the fact specific asset
exit_rule: Two attempts with no reply, then closed.
advanced_rules: No new fact means no message. This is enforced, not advisory.

who_they_are: Anyone who has already paid us and is past 60 percent of their course.
what_they_want: To finish what they started, and sometimes to add the piece their qualification does not cover.
whats_stopping_them: Exam pressure. Fatigue. Fee for the next level.
how_to_spot_them: A match against the student master, plus course progress.
what_to_offer: The next level, or the practical skills programme, at a combined price where one genuinely exists.
what_to_say: Continuity. What comes next and why now, framed around what they have already done.
what_not_to_say: Never use an acquisition opening. Never sell to a student who is behind schedule or has a complaint open.
next_action: Send the progression or skills asset. Student Success calls, not a new lead counsellor.
cadence: Once a week, and never during their exam window.
exit_rule: One repeat after their exam window, then stop for 90 days.
advanced_rules: Hard block if progress is behind schedule or a support ticket is open.

who_they_are: A parent enquiring on behalf of a student, at any stage.
what_they_want: Certainty that this is a safe decision for their child, and a clear total cost.
whats_stopping_them: They did not study this themselves, so they cannot judge it. Cost across all levels is unclear.
how_to_spot_them: Parent language on the form or in the reply, or a decision maker recorded as parent.
what_to_offer: The full route with total cost and outcomes, plus a joint counselling slot with the student.
what_to_say: Outcomes and total cost, answered before anything else.
what_not_to_say: No student slang. No peer proof. No urgency. No discount language.
next_action: Offer the parent guide or an evening call, and let them choose which.
priority: Call this week, in the evening window
cadence: Every 3 days, evening sends only, two attempts maximum.
exit_rule: Two attempts, then park with a standing invitation.
advanced_rules: Parents respond badly to persistence. Two attempts is a hard cap.

who_they_are: Anyone failing an eligibility rule or asking for a course that is the wrong step for them right now.
what_they_want: The course they asked for, which they cannot have yet.
whats_stopping_them: A rule they did not know about, or a sequence they misunderstood.
how_to_spot_them: Eligibility check failed, or the course is too early or too late for their stage.
what_to_offer: The nearest course that is genuinely open to them now, plus the sequence to the one they wanted.
what_to_say: The rule, plainly, then the open route. No apology and no workaround.
what_not_to_say: Never sell around an awarding body rule. Never imply an exception exists.
next_action: State the reason, name the open course, offer the sequence written out.
cadence: Two touches, then a dated return at the eligibility window.
owner: System, counsellor if the case is complex
exit_rule: Two attempts, then park with a dated return.
advanced_rules: No payment link may be issued to this playbook under any circumstances.

who_they_are: Anyone opted out, unreachable, already converted, duplicated, or under a legal hold.
what_to_say: Nothing. At most one confirmation that we have stopped.
next_action: Stop. Confirm once if they asked to stop, then never again.
exit_rule: Immediate and permanent until documented re consent.
advanced_rules: This overrides every other rule in the system.
